l4_steps.name: Extract gate event data from AMS
l4_steps.output: Raw gate event log: block-in, block-out, stand assignment, delays
l4_steps.kpi: Data extraction latency ≤15 min after period close
l4_steps.pain_point: AMS event timestamps may be entered manually by ramp agents, introducing ±3 min inaccuracies that distort D0 calculations; no auto-capture at many regional stations

l4_steps.name: Pull ACARS turnaround event timestamps
l4_steps.input: AMS gate event log from step 1.1
l4_steps.output: ACARS-corroborated block times: chocks-on, door-open, door-close, push-back
l4_steps.kpi: ACARS coverage ≥95% of narrowbody turns at hub stations
l4_steps.pain_point: Regional and outstations with older ground equipment may have ACARS downlink gaps; fallback to manual log creates 5–8% data voids that inflate reported OTP

l4_steps.name: Ingest baggage handling data from BRS
l4_steps.input: Baggage reconciliation system (BRS) export for the period
l4_steps.output: Baggage mishandling records: late bags, wrong-loaded, offloaded, damaged
l4_steps.pain_point: WorldTracer data latency at transborder stations (US/Canada/Mexico) can exceed 4 hours due to customs hold scanning delays, making same-day reporting unreliable

l4_steps.name: Validate data completeness across all stations
l4_steps.input: Merged AMS, ACARS, and WorldTracer datasets loaded to Redshift staging schema
l4_steps.output: Data quality report: missing records flagged, coverage % per station
l4_steps.kpi: Data completeness ≥98% of operated flights before KPI run proceeds
l4_steps.pain_point: Redshift ingestion pipelines from SITA AMS rely on SFTP batch files; file delivery failures at outstations can silently drop entire station's data from the reporting run

l4_steps.name: Calculate D0 and D15 on-time departure metrics
l4_steps.input: Validated gate event dataset from phase 1
l4_steps.output: D0 and D15 departure performance % per station, per fleet type, per hour-of-day
l4_steps.pain_point: Carrier-caused vs. non-carrier delay classification is applied post-hoc via delay codes entered by agents — code 93 (ATC) vs code 15 (late aircraft) misclassification inflates ground ops performance metrics

l4_steps.name: Compute gate and stand utilisation rate
l4_steps.input: Stand assignment and block-time data from AMS
l4_steps.output: Gate utilisation % per stand per day; peak-hour congestion index per station
l4_steps.kpi: Gate utilisation target ≥72% at primary hub gates; congestion index <1.2 at peak
l4_steps.pain_point: AMS stand assignment data does not reflect real-time remote-stand tows, causing gate utilisation to be overstated for aerobridged stands and understated for remote apron positions

l4_steps.name: Calculate baggage mishandling and delivery KPIs
l4_steps.input: Baggage mishandling records from step 1.3; passenger boarding counts from Amadeus Altéa PSS
l4_steps.output: Mishandled baggage rate per 1,000 passengers; average delivery-to-belt time (minutes)
l4_steps.kpi: Mishandled bag rate ≤3.5 per 1,000 pax (IATA World Baggage Report benchmark); first-bag-to-belt ≤20 min
l4_steps.pain_point: WorldTracer only captures reported mishandled bags; unreported incidents (bag on wrong belt, passenger retrieves wrong bag) are invisible to the KPI, creating systematic under-reporting at busy stations

l4_steps.name: Assess computed KPIs against threshold rules
l4_steps.input: Computed KPI values from steps 2.1–2.3; threshold configuration table in Redshift
l4_steps.output: KPI status flags: Green / Amber / Red per metric per station
l4_steps.kpi: 100% of KPI metrics receive a RAG status within 30 min of data validation
l4_steps.pain_point: Threshold rules are stored as hardcoded SQL in Redshift procedures; changes require a DBA ticket and 48-hour change-management approval — preventing rapid threshold adjustment during irregular ops (IROPS) periods

l4_steps.name: Build station scorecard dashboard in Tableau
l4_steps.input: RAG-flagged KPI dataset published to Tableau Server data source
l4_steps.output: Interactive station scorecard: D0/D15, gate util, bag KPIs, trend sparklines per station
l4_steps.kpi: Scorecard refresh latency ≤60 min after reporting period close
l4_steps.pain_point: Tableau Server extract refresh contention at period close (multiple dashboards refreshing simultaneously) causes 30–90 min delays in scorecard availability, frustrating station managers on early shifts

l4_steps.name: Identify underperforming stations via threshold alerts
l4_steps.input: Published station scorecard with RAG flags
l4_steps.output: Underperformer shortlist: stations with ≥2 Red KPIs or single critical-metric Red flag
l4_steps.kpi: Underperformer identification completed within 2 hours of scorecard publication
l4_steps.pain_point: Alert logic in Tableau uses static thresholds that do not account for seasonal demand variation — stations operating above-plan capacity in peak periods are incorrectly flagged Red, creating alert fatigue

l4_steps.name: Conduct root cause drill-down for Red-flagged stations
l4_steps.input: Underperformer shortlist; flight-level delay code breakdown from Redshift
l4_steps.output: Root cause classification: staffing, equipment, aircraft late-in, ATC, weather, process
l4_steps.kpi: Root cause assigned for ≥90% of Red-flagged stations within 4 hours
l4_steps.pain_point: Delay code data quality (entered by ramp agents under time pressure) is insufficient for reliable root cause analysis — IATA AHM delay code 15 (late aircraft arrival) frequently masks ground-caused delays

l4_steps.name: Issue performance improvement notice to station manager
l4_steps.input: Root cause classification and supporting KPI evidence from step 3.3
l4_steps.output: Performance Improvement Notice (PIN) with specific KPI targets and 30-day remediation timeline
l4_steps.kpi: PIN issued within 24 hours of Red-flag identification for stations with ground-caused root cause
l4_steps.pain_point: PINs are issued via email with no structured tracking system — follow-up compliance is manual, leading to 40% of PINs having no documented station response within the 30-day window

l4_steps.name: Assess whether VP Ground Ops escalation is required
l4_steps.input: Station KPI trend data; PIN issuance history; escalation threshold ruleset
l4_steps.output: Escalation decision: escalate to VP Ground Ops or manage at performance manager level
l4_steps.kpi: Escalation decision made within 48 hours of Red-flag identification
l4_steps.pain_point: Escalation thresholds are not codified — decisions rely on individual manager judgement, leading to inconsistent escalation behaviour across regions and delayed VP awareness of systemic station failures

l4_steps.name: Brief VP Ground Ops with station performance summary
l4_steps.input: Escalated station performance package: KPI trend, root cause, PIN history, remediation plan
l4_steps.output: VP decision: resource reallocation, contractor review, or formal station audit trigger
l4_steps.kpi: VP briefing delivered within 72 hours of escalation trigger
l4_steps.pain_point: VP briefing packs are manually compiled from Tableau exports and email threads — no single-source-of-truth system means briefing preparation takes 4–6 hours and version mismatches occur between analyst and manager copies

l4_steps.name: Publish daily ops performance briefing
l4_steps.input: Overnight KPI computation run; previous-day baseline
l4_steps.output: Daily Ops Briefing email/dashboard: top-5 KPI movers, Red-flag summary, delay code distribution
l4_steps.kpi: Daily briefing distributed by 07:00 local time at each hub station
l4_steps.pain_point: Tableau Server scheduled subscription emails require SMTP relay through corporate IT — relay outages (averaging 2 per month) cause delayed or failed briefing delivery with no automatic retry or fallback channel

l4_steps.name: Distribute weekly station scorecard to station managers
l4_steps.input: 7-day rolling KPI dataset; prior week scorecard for trend comparison
l4_steps.output: Weekly scorecard PDF distributed to station managers and regional directors
l4_steps.kpi: Weekly scorecard delivered every Monday by 09:00 local hub time
l4_steps.pain_point: Scorecard distribution list is maintained manually in a shared Excel file — personnel changes at stations result in stale distribution lists, with outgoing managers receiving reports and replacement managers missing them for up to 4 weeks

l4_steps.name: Submit monthly KPI report to senior leadership
l4_steps.input: Monthly KPI summary from Redshift; incident log from AMS; financial impact data from SAP S/4HANA Finance
l4_steps.output: Monthly Ground Ops Performance Report: trend charts, YoY comparison, cost-of-poor-quality estimate
l4_steps.kpi: Monthly report submitted to SVP Operations by the 5th calendar day of the following month
l4_steps.pain_point: Integrating financial cost data from SAP S/4HANA with operational KPI data from Redshift requires a manual reconciliation step — no automated connector exists between operational and financial data layers

l4_steps.name: Analyse 13-week rolling performance trends
l4_steps.input: 13-week historical KPI dataset from Redshift; seasonality index from Amadeus SkyCAST
l4_steps.output: Trend analysis report: directional KPI movement, seasonal-adjusted performance, benchmark gap
l4_steps.kpi: Trend analysis completed quarterly; covers 100% of hub and focus-city stations
l4_steps.pain_point: Seasonal demand data from Amadeus SkyCAST is available to network planning but not integrated into the ground ops reporting layer — analysts apply manual seasonality adjustments based on prior-year data, introducing estimation error

l4_steps.name: Review and update KPI targets in BI platform
l4_steps.input: 13-week trend report; benchmark data from IATA AHM and Airport Council International (ACI)
l4_steps.output: Updated KPI threshold configuration approved and published to Tableau data source; change log entry
l4_steps.kpi: KPI targets reviewed at minimum quarterly; changes approved within 5 business days of review
l4_steps.pain_point: KPI thresholds stored in Tableau data sources cannot be version-controlled — rollback after an erroneous threshold change requires DBA intervention to restore a Redshift snapshot, causing 4–8 hours of incorrect reporting
